title: Marginal logistic regression by GEE on clustered binary data
summary: Estimates a MARGINAL odds ratio when outcomes are correlated within clinic, and reports both the model-based and the sandwich standard error because packages disagree about which one to print.
_marginal_not_conditional: GEE estimates the POPULATION-AVERAGE odds ratio. mixed-effects-logistic-clustered estimates the CLUSTER-CONDITIONAL one, and on the same data those are different numbers -- the marginal is attenuated toward the null. Neither is a better version of the other and a plan must say which it wants. That is why this entry's fixture generates the marginal model directly rather than through a random intercept: asking GEE to recover a conditional parameter would measure the attenuation and call it error.
_few_clusters: This fixture has 90 clusters. The sandwich variance is a large-sample estimator and is biased DOWNWARD with few clusters -- CLAUDE.md's rule warns under 30 and blocks under 15 unless a small-sample approach is named. An entry demonstrating the sandwich on 12 clusters would be modelling the practice the product warns about. Small-sample corrections (Mancl-DeRouen, Kauermann-Carroll, Fay-Graubard) are a separate entry and are not in geepack.
pinned_defaults: R: the data are sorted by cluster before fitting. geeglm requires observations from one cluster to be contiguous, does not check, and silently treats unsorted input as many small clusters.
Python: cov_struct=Exchangeable(). statsmodels DEFAULTS TO Independence().
Python: statsmodels does NOT require sorted input, which is a difference from R that a translated file loses.
SAS: type=exch. PROC GENMOD's REPEATED statement DEFAULTS TO type=ind.
SAS: model outcome(event='1'). GENMOD models the probability of the FIRST ordered level, which for a 0/1 variable is zero, so omitting this reverses the sign of every coefficient with no warning.
SAS: modelse, so the model-based table is printed beside the empirical one.
Stata: corr(exchangeable) IS xtgee's default and is written out anyway, because it is the only one of the four that defaults this way.
Stata: vce(robust) is NOT the default. xtgee reports the MODEL-BASED standard error unless asked, while the other three report the sandwich.
